question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed experimental one-Claw-per-new-agent package contract, including its CLI, manifest, ownership, provenance, update, and removal semantics?
rationale: The patch is an RFC whose durable user and plugin-facing contracts cannot be validated or accepted by documentation review alone; maintainers must choose the supported product boundary.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC as a draft while the linked experimental implementation work provides more operational and upgrade evidence.

options.title: Accept the scoped contract
options.body: Approve the experimental contract, create the implementation issue, set the RFC status to accepted, and merge the documentation.

options.title: Narrow the first release
options.body: Approve only a smaller initial package lifecycle and defer selected update, export, MCP, cron, or shared-resource semantics.

recommendation.title: Continue incubation
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC as a draft while the linked experimental implementation work provides more operational and upgrade evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review supplied the current product model, and the remaining decision concerns that model's permanent scope.
